jobs.title: Associate, Private Debt
jobs.description:
Founded in 1999, Audax Group is a leading alternative investment manager with offices in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London and Hong Kong. With approximately $42 billion of assets under management and more than 475 employees, Audax is a leading capital partner for middle market companies, operating through three business lines: Audax Private Equity, Audax Private Debt, and Audax Strategic Capital.

For more information, visit www.audaxgroup.com or follow Audax Group on LinkedIn .

Since its founding in 2000, Audax Private Debt has partnered with leading private equity firms to help finance their purchase of middle market companies. We provide senior loans, unitranche loans and junior capital in addition to co-investments in equity securities. We source opportunities directly from financial sponsors throughout North America, investing in leveraged buyouts, acquisition financings and debt recapitalizations. We differentiate ourselves by taking a long-term view as it relates to new financings and portfolio decisions. Audax Private Debt has an established track record of helping private equity firms acquire and grow businesses.

We are based in New York City and have 50+ investment professionals. Our leadership team has been in place since inception and our managing directors average 25 years of investment experience.

Position Summary

The Associate will serve as an integral member of the Audax Private Debt investment team, supporting the underwriting of new first lien senior secured loan investments and the ongoing monitoring of portfolio companies across Audax Private Debt portfolios. This role offers broad exposure to the entire investment lifecycle, including transaction evaluation, due diligence, financial modeling, deal execution, portfolio management, and investment committee processes.

This position provides a unique opportunity to join a highly collaborative and entrepreneurial team while developing expertise across credit investing, financial analysis, industry research, risk assessment, debt financing, and portfolio management.

Key Responsibilities

Investment Underwriting & Due Diligence

- Analyze and evaluate investment opportunities supporting sponsor-backed leveraged buyout transactions.

- Conduct detailed industry, market, customer, and competitive analyses to assess investment opportunities.

- Build, review, and maintain complex financial models, including forecasting, leverage, liquidity, and downside analyses.

- Evaluate alternative capital structures and investment terms to determine appropriate risk-adjusted returns.

Deal Execution & Investment Committee Process

- Participate in all stages of transaction execution from initial screening through closing.

- Prepare investment memoranda, presentations, and supporting materials for investment committee review.

- Clearly communicate investment recommendations and credit views through written analyses and verbal presentations.

Portfolio Management & Monitoring

- Monitor a portfolio of existing investments, including financial performance, compliance, ratings activity, amendments, waivers, and market developments.

- Analyze amendment requests, refinancing opportunities, add-on investments, and secondary market opportunities.

- Monitor industry trends and market developments that could affect portfolio performance.

Qualifications

Required Experience

- Bachelor’s degree required.

- 2 - 4 years of experience in investment banking, direct lending, private credit, structured credit, leveraged finance, or a related field.

- Experience developing and utilizing detailed financial models.

- LBO/ sponsor transaction exposure

- Experience analyzing leveraged transactions and corporate credit risk preferred.

- Experience with credit committee exposure and investment memo preparation preferred.

Skills & Competencies

- Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.

- Ability to assess the credit quality and risk profile of potential investments.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentation experience.

- Strong work ethic and demonstrated desire to learn and develop professionally.

- Ability to thrive in a collaborative, team-oriented environment.

- Strong academic record.

Why Audax

Audax offers a unique opportunity to join a growing and entrepreneurial private debt platform with exposure to all aspects of the investment process. Team members gain hands-on experience in credit underwriting, financial analysis, industry research, debt financing, transaction execution, and portfolio company management while working alongside experienced investment professionals in a supportive, collegial, and high-performing environment.

LOCATION:

New York, New York.  4 days/week in office. These office requirements may change based on the needs of the business.

jobs.title: Director Financial Planning & Analysis, Family Office
jobs.description:
Founded in 1999, Audax Group is a leading alternative investment manager with offices in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London and Hong Kong. With approximately $42 billion of assets under management and more than 475 employees, Audax is a leading capital partner for middle market companies, operating through three business lines: Audax Private Equity, Audax Private Debt, and Audax Strategic Capital.

For more information, visit www.audaxgroup.com or follow Audax Group on LinkedIn .

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, leads the financial planning, reporting, tax coordination, and investment administration functions for the family office . This individual serves as the principal financial point of contact for the family, overseeing recurring reporting cycles, tax strategy execution, investment diligence and administration, and supporting estate and wealth transfer planning in close partnership with outside tax, legal, and investment advisors.

The ideal candidate is a self-starter with expertise across financial planning, tax, and investment administration, capable of managing complex and highly confidential information while driving process improvement. This role requires exceptional attention to detail, sound financial judgment, and the discretion to manage sensitive personal financial matters directly with the family's principals and outside advisors.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Reporting & Cash Management (Approx. 25%):

- Oversee preparation and review of recurring reporting deliverables, including weekly consolidated cash reporting, monthly unfunded-commitment reporting, and quarterly net asset and investment schedules across all reporting entities

- Direct the build and maintenance of the 10-year financial projection model, including the bridge reconciling projections to the weekly cash position

- Manage the annual budgeting cycle and monthly budget-to-actual reporting, providing high-level review and commentary for principal review

- Oversee quarterly reporting for family trusts and related entities, and coordinate monthly and inception-to-date reporting for donor-advised fund activity

- Respond to and manage ad hoc financial reporting requests as they arise

Tax Strategy & Compliance (Approx. 20%):

- Own the quarterly estimated tax payment process, working directly with outside tax advisors to determine current-quarter payments and revise full-year forecasts; review and approve recommendations before submission to principals

- Maintain and review the annual tax summary model, ensuring it reconciles to underlying K-1 and entity-level trackers

- Lead the annual tax return review process: populate and validate draft return data against the tax model, identify variances, and manage resolution with outside preparers

Investment Management Support (Approx. 20%):

- Lead diligence coordination on new investment opportunities: circulate data room materials, evaluate commitment timing and constraints, assess qualified small business stock (QSBS) eligibility, and determine appropriate investing entity structure, including use of blocker entities

- Manage execution of new investments, including submission of indications of interest, coordination of legal review, and completion of subscription documentation

- Ensure consistent attendance and note-taking at existing portfolio company and manager update calls/meetings, with timely circulation of summaries

- Review monthly liquid manager performance reporting

- Evaluate and make recommendations on discrete investment decisions, tracking performance against relevant benchmarks

Estate & Wealth Transfer Planning Support (Approx. 15%):

- Partner with estate counsel and principals to plan and execute estate documentation changes, including trustee and beneficiary updates and trust restructurings, including any required financial modeling

- Prepare materials and agendas for principal planning meetings; maintain supporting asset-change summaries and meeting documentation

- Model proposed estate and gifting strategies and present options to principals to support decision-making

- Review annual estate plan models and periodic estate plan summary presentations prepared by other team members

- Oversee administrative execution of estate vehicles

- Coordinate the transfer of legal ownership of assets into current trust structures across accounts and investments, including required legal review

- Track and review annual life insurance policy performance and premium payment recommendations in coordination with outside brokers

Gifting & Lifetime Exemption Planning (Approx. 10%):

- Maintain tracking of remaining lifetime gift and generation-skipping transfer (GST) exemption for each principal, updating as taxable gifts occur

- Coordinate annual education-savings (529/UTMA) funding recommendations and update tracking based on actual contribution activity

- Prepare the annual gifting overview summarizing gifting completed to date and remaining opportunities ahead of year-end

- Compile underlying data for annual gift tax returns, review draft returns for accuracy against source files, and obtain required legal sign-off before filing

Credit Facilities (Approx. 5%):

- Manage external lines of credit, including covenant compliance preparation, collateral monitoring, market comparison ahead of renewals, and negotiation of terms

- Oversee internal intra-family loan and line-of-credit tracking, ensuring draws and interest payments are applied and recorded correctly

Special Projects & Other (Approx. 5%):

- Evaluate financing options and monthly carrying costs for major family purchases (e.g., real estate) and recommend optimal funding structures

- Administer entity-level investment vehicles, including tracking interest payments and coordinating with property/investment managers on tax payments and cash sweeps

- Take on additional special projects and analyses as directed by principals

COMPETENCIES:

- Strong analytical and modeling capabilities with the ability to synthesize complex financial, tax, and legal information into actionable recommendations.

- Excellent communication skills and comfort working directly with principals, outside counsel, and third-party advisors.

- High attention to detail with a demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams and deadlines.

- Strong leadership presence, with the ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment on sensitive matters.

- Exceptional discretion in handling highly confidential personal and financial information.

- Proactive and adaptable in a dynamic, relationship-driven environment.

REQUIREMENTS/QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor's degree in finance, Accounting, or a related field; CPA, CFA, or MBA preferred.

- 8+ years of progressive experience in a family office, private wealth platform, alternative investment manager, public accounting firm, or related financial services environment, ideally supporting high-net-worth individuals and families

- Demonstrated experience leading complex financial planning, forecasting, liquidity, and executive reporting processes; advanced financial modeling skills required.

- Strong technical grounding in personal and entity-level tax concepts, trust and estate structures, and investment fund mechanics (capital calls, K-1s, QSBS, blocker entities).

- Experience with Anaplan, Investran, and PowerBI is a strong plus.

- Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and demonstrated financial modeling experience, including long-range projection models.

- Proven experience coordinating with outside advisors (tax, legal, investment) and managing complex, cross-functional workstreams to completion.

jobs.title: Finance Manager, Private Debt
jobs.description:
Founded in 1999, Audax Group is a leading alternative investment manager with offices in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London and Hong Kong. With approximately $42 billion of assets under management and more than 475 employees, Audax is a leading capital partner for middle market companies, operating through three business lines: Audax Private Equity, Audax Private Debt, and Audax Strategic Capital.

For more information, visit www.audaxgroup.com or follow Audax Group on LinkedIn .

Based in New York, Audax Private Debt is a leading debt capital partner for North American middle market companies. Since its inception in 2000, the firm has invested more than $42 billion in support of over 290 private equity sponsors. Audax Private Debt works collaboratively to build tailored financing solutions for its clients through a comprehensive range of offerings that includes first lien, stretch senior, unitranche, second lien, and subordinated debt, as well as equity co-investments. Audax Private Debt is an experienced and trusted partner with senior leadership averaging more than 26 years in private credit and 15 years working together at the firm through multiple economic cycles. For more information, please visit  audaxprivatedebt.com  or follow us on  LinkedIn .

POSITION SUMMARY:

The position is responsible for the financial reporting and accounting for Audax Private Debt based in Boston . The Finance Manager is also a key contributor to the Private Debt valuation process and is responsible for the compliance and control processes related to several Private Debt Funds. Private Debt invests in debt securities of middle market companies backed by private equity sponsors via a variety of different investment vehicles. The candidate will work closely with the Valuation, Investor Relations, CLO, FP&A, Tax and Senior Debt Deal teams.

The ideal candidate is a self-motivated and detail-oriented team player who will thrive in a fast-paced environment and must be able to prioritize and complete all projects with precision in a timely manner. As Audax Private Debt continues to grow, the position will evolve with the direction of the business’ needs.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

- Preparation and review of the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, fund level returns and investor deliverables for various Private Debt funds

- Work with the Investor Relations team in preparing fundraising materials and in providing information for investor requests, including fund performance data, fee information and underlying portfolio financial information

- Prepare monthly and quarterly MD&A on fund performance for senior management

- Contribute to the valuation process for debt, equity and CLO investments

- Review fund administrator’s work on various Private Debt funds

- Administration of assigned funds: prepare/review, coordinate, calculate capital calls and distributions

- Work with the Tax team in preparing quarterly tax estimates as well as year-end tax allocations

- Track and update the portfolio of investments for the various Private Debt funds

- Track interest payment receipts across portfolio team

- Daily cash management, monitoring, and reconciliation with the bank

- Take a lead role with the firm’s outside auditor in preparation/review of year-end audited financials

- Be available to provide timely communication to internal and external stakeholders on projects when required

- Responsible for coaching and developing junior team members

COMPETENCIES:

- Advanced GAAP financial reporting experience

- Effective communication skills and ability interact with Senior Management and outside parties

- Strong organizational skills

- Professional and energetic attitude

- Expert knowledge of Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, etc.)

- Self-starter with ability to work independently and in a team environment

- Exemplary leadership skills

- Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage competing priorities

- Demonstrated consistency in meeting deadlines with quality work product

REQUIREMENTS/QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting/Finance with a CPA

- 5 plus years of experience, including public accounting, preferably focusing on alternative investment asset managers

- Extensive experience with Private Equity/Debt valuation
